imports.replacement: Import exact Symbols from rxjs/<capability> and invoke source[symbol](...). Use rxjs/pipe only for deliberate Symbol composition.
imports.rationale: RxJS Next does not publish the RxJS 7 pipeable-function or string-named .pipe surface.

imports.replacement: Use the active realm's ambient Observable and Subscriber after @rxjs/observable-polyfill initialization when needed.
imports.rationale: The platform owns these constructors; the rxjs root does not re-export compatibility classes for them.

imports.replacement: Use @rxjs/test rxTest() and its explicit cold(), hot(), observable(), virtual host-time, and assertion helpers.
imports.rationale: The public scheduler classes and manual TestScheduler mode are not part of the Next runtime or test contract.

imports.replacement: Use platform fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventTarget.when, or an application adapter selected for the required cancellation and sharing contract.
imports.rationale: RxJS Next does not currently publish the RxJS 7 DOM specialty packages or their wrapper types.

imports.replacement: Replace with an accepted public Next subpath or application-owned code after semantic review.
imports.rationale: RxJS 7 internals are not preserved as public package contracts and must not be revived to satisfy migration tests.

imports.replacement: Wrap callback or resource ownership explicitly with Observable and AbortSignal; use platform conversion or capability-specific mappings where applicable.
imports.rationale: No accepted public Next function preserves these RxJS 7 imports and complete overload contracts.

imports.replacement: Use platform error and AbortSignal reason handling or an application-owned aggregate error contract.
imports.rationale: These errors belong to removed RxJS 7 Subscription and closed-Subject internals.

types.replacement: Use ordinary typed functions with exact Symbol invocation or rxjs/pipe composition.
types.rationale: RxJS Next does not publish the pipeable-operator type family.

types.replacement: Use AbortController, AbortSignal, SubscribeOptions, and Subscriber.addTeardown inside producers.
types.rationale: subscribe() returns undefined and cancellation is signal-owned; no Subscription facade is published.

types.replacement: Use the ambient ObservableValue/platform Observable.from input contract and review custom inputs manually.
types.rationale: The platform conversion boundary deliberately excludes arbitrary subscribables and legacy observable interop.

types.replacement: Use ambient Observer/Subscriber shapes or the concrete intentional Subject/connectable APIs; define application protocols locally when needed.
types.rationale: These RxJS 7 helper interfaces are not a public Next import family.

types.replacement: Use host timing APIs, Date.now-compatible narrow providers where explicitly documented, and @rxjs/test virtual host time.
types.rationale: There is no general public scheduler abstraction in RxJS Next.

types.replacement: Use inference from the accepted Next API or application-owned utility types; do not deep-import RxJS internals.
types.rationale: These RxJS 7 implementation-facing inference helpers are not stable Next public types.

types.replacement: Use the structural keyed group view, structural timestamp result, or TimeInterval exported by the exact rxjs/time-interval capability as applicable.
types.rationale: The RxJS 7 root type imports are not preserved even where a capability exposes an intentional structural or subpath-specific result.

schedulers.replacement: Use virtualizable host timing and task APIs; use @rxjs/test for deterministic tests.
schedulers.rationale: RxJS Next does not publish scheduler instances or scheduler classes.

schedulers.replacement: Remove only an explicitly classified scheduler overload and verify ordering with host-time behavior; otherwise retain the source and stop automation.
schedulers.rationale: Current capabilities use host scheduling or narrow clock providers, and the port harness adapter is not a production SchedulerLike contract.

interop.replacement: Expose a platform-supported ObservableValue category or wrap the source explicitly in the active realm.
interop.rationale: Legacy observable interop is outside the accepted platform Observable.from contract.

interop.replacement: Write an explicit application adapter that owns cancellation and terminal behavior, or choose a supported platform input category.
interop.rationale: The 15 executable compatibility-only failures deliberately preserve this unsupported input boundary.

interop.replacement: Initialize each realm independently and bridge values through an explicit application protocol.
interop.rationale: RxJS does not traverse realms or promise generic Symbol borrowing onto unrelated receivers.

interop.replacement: Use exact Symbol composition and the versioned derived-construction protocol through supported public capabilities.
interop.rationale: The RxJS 7 lift/source/operator protocol is removed and is not a public Next subclass hook.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Use combineLatestAll, exhaustMap(identity), mergeMap, or Observable[partition] respectively.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: The deprecated RxJS 7 names are not public Next Symbol identities; migration uses their canonical accepted mappings.
The deprecated creation functions are not retained as callable Next aliases.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Use map with a constant or property projection, or the corresponding canonical flattening Symbol with an explicit projection.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: Migration may preserve behavior through exact mappings, but the deprecated pipeable function/import shape is not supported.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Use the accepted unified or With-form exact Symbol and its documented source-array/result-selector mapping.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: Legacy pipeable aliases are migration inputs, not preserved function exports.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Prefer share, shareReplay, connect, or connectable with an explicit connector/reset contract; exact legacy-named Symbols remain migration evidence, not a compatibility promise.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: Producer sharing, replay, reset, and ref-count semantics require explicit lifecycle review.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Use behaviorSubject(value), replaySubject({ size, maxAge }), or the advanced PerSubscriptionSubjectBase only for a justified custom hot Subject.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: D-050 stabilizes lowercase factories and removes the misleading ColdSubject name without aliases.

deprecatedAliases.replacement: Use one of iterateEachValue, iterateBufferedValues, iterateLatestValue, or iterateNextValue from its exact Symbol subpath.
deprecatedAliases.rationale: The exploratory standalone helpers were removed so buffering and dropping policy stays explicit.
